quickAnswer.title: From CTC to take-home pay
quickAnswer.question: How do I estimate in-hand salary from CTC?
quickAnswer.answer: Start with gross monthly pay. Subtract your employee provident fund (PF), income tax withheld (TDS), professional tax and other payroll deductions. The CTC on your offer can also include employer PF, gratuity, insurance and bonuses outside regular monthly pay.
quickAnswer.formula: Estimated take-home = monthly gross pay − employee PF − estimated TDS − professional tax − other payroll deductions
quickAnswer.note: Educational estimate only. Check your offer letter and payslip before relying on the result.

contentSections.heading: What CTC, gross pay and take-home mean
contentSections.body: CTC is what your employer budgets for your pay and benefits. Gross pay is your cash salary before deductions. Take-home is the amount that reaches your bank account.
bullets: Your offer can include employer PF, gratuity, insurance and bonuses as part of CTC.
Your payslip shows deductions from gross pay, including employee PF, income tax and professional tax.

contentSections.heading: Compare tax regimes and job offers
contentSections.body: The Quick calculator computes tax from your salary and eligible deductions. Keep the salary inputs the same when comparing tax regimes. Use the Salary cash planner to compare offers month by month when bonuses, a delayed first pay or switching costs matter.

faqs.question: Does HRA increase in-hand salary?
faqs.answer: HRA can be part of your gross pay. Whether any of it is exempt from tax depends on your tax regime, rent, salary and location.

faqs.question: Is gratuity deducted from my monthly salary?
faqs.answer: Gratuity in your CTC usually shows an employer cost. Check your offer to see how it is listed and your payslip to see your actual monthly deductions.

faqs.question: Why should I compare tax regimes before estimating in-hand salary?
faqs.answer: Your tax regime changes the estimated tax deducted from your pay. Compare both with the same salary, using only deductions you qualify for. Your employer may withhold a different amount.

salary-in-hand-calculator-india.formulaExplanation: Start with the monthly gross pay shown by the calculator. Subtract employee PF, estimated monthly income tax (TDS), professional tax and other payroll deductions to get your estimated take-home pay.
salary-in-hand-calculator-india.example: Suppose your annual CTC is ₹12 lakh and your monthly basic pay is ₹50,000. With employer PF of ₹6,000 a month included in CTC, gross pay is ₹94,000 a month. Subtract ₹6,000 employee PF and ₹200 professional tax. With no other income or deductions and ₹0 estimated income tax under the new regime for Tax Year 2026–27, take-home is ₹87,800 a month. This example assumes both PF contributions are 12% of full basic pay and the package has no other employer costs or separate bonuses.
howToUse: Enter your fixed annual pay from the offer. Leave out bonuses paid separately, gratuity, insurance and other costs that do not reach you as regular pay.
Use basic pay from your offer or payslip. If you know it, turn off the automatic estimate and enter annual basic pay as a percentage of the annual amount you entered.
Check whether employer PF is already in that amount. Set your employee PF rate, professional tax and other monthly deductions using your payslip.
Select your tax year and regime. Use the monthly breakdown to check gross pay, estimated tax and take-home. For the old regime, enter only rent and deductions you qualify for.
assumptions: The Quick calculator assumes employer PF is 12% of basic pay when you include it in CTC. It applies your employee PF rate to full basic pay. If your employer caps PF or uses a different wage base, check the actual amounts with payroll.
Monthly tax is an estimate based on salary and the year and regime you select. Actual withholding can change with bonuses, declarations or earlier income.
The Quick calculator excludes the surcharge on taxable income above ₹50 lakh. Use the income tax calculator for an estimate that includes the salary surcharge.
